items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: So I took him under my wing and taught him to read, man, and the guy just blew.

ctx.x: He thinks he can play, you know. So I said, 'Okay,' I said, 'Well, we're going to play some things.' I said, 'What do you want to play?' He said, 'What do you want to play?' So this got me guy. He said, 'Let's play something up.' That meant fast, you know what I'm saying. I said, 'Well, how about a little I Got Rhythm?' He says, 'Solid, man.' He struck out on it, man, and this cat blew the bells off, and after that first, man, so I decided to slip a little music in front of him, you know, the section. It was…

So I took him under my wing and taught him to read, man, and the guy just blew. And we made trips one nighters, and he broke it up, and he was in my band for quite a few years. Then, of course, I would always tell my brother, you know, about anybody great like that. And when I rejoined my brother, I took Roy with me, and we got this Chicago job at the Grand Terrace -- Roy Eldridge and Chu Berry and joined John Fletcher, and, of course, there was quite a story behind that, you know. John Fletcher was broadcasting,…

" Christopher Columbus " as the theme song. Roy was in that band, and he really played. And funny thing about it, just a few weeks ago we were right here in Denver reminiscing, all this, all of those old times, and, well, since Roy was with me, you know, he toured with Basie and went to Europe on his own with Lockjaw Davis, you know, about seven pieces, small group. They broke it up. And, of course, he's got places where he can play anytime, you know, and he's traveled extensively, and he's just matured quite a…

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: Because he brought me in his band, and I told him, 'I can't read.' He says, 'You'll be all right,' you know.

ctx.x: Well, actually, what got me started was the trumpet player that was in my brother's band, a ...(?)... named Archie Johnson. He was a killer, man, you know. Then Rex came and stayed at our house, and he showed me a couple of breaks. Man, he was really my idol. I mean, like I couldn't... I didn't dig it because I didn't get fat like he was, you know, so I could look like him. I started to do everything he did, you know. When he came in with Fletcher, he got me and took me, and he set behind me and he's showing what…

But really the one that instilled the thing about being competitive and wanting to cut people was Horace Henderson. I give that cat all the credit in the world. I never mentioned that, but he needs some credit. Because he brought me in his band, and I told him, 'I can't read.' He says, 'You'll be all right,' you know. And I played third, and somehow or other, I could come up with the third part, you know.
